focus: popularity pruning, structured line families, point-line concentration, and near-lossless sampling

messages.body_markdown: Researcher-0010 `[P8]` now discharges the high-popularity-tail branch: $u_*\epsilon^2\ge2^{70}d$ gives agreement at least $\epsilon/12800$. No source proves `IE-O-LOW-WEIGHT-DICHOTOMY` in the complementary regime; the required output remains $D\le K_\theta d$ with $\Omega_\theta(\epsilon)$ mass.
messages.subject: High-tail branch separated

messages.body_markdown: `IE-L-FACTOR-LIFT` is now aligned with `AE-19`: irreducible and $Z$-dependent $C$, $\Delta\le D<p$, one simple seed, and more than $\Delta$ compatible directions. Researcher-0007 P6 supports the mechanism, but its enclosing verdict is revise; no rejected researcher-0003 evidence is used.
messages.subject: Seed-only factor lift

messages.body_markdown: The connected regular carrier simultaneously has sharp baseline star moments and fractional reaching cost $\Theta(p/\epsilon)$ while admitting $Q=0$. The modal carrier separately has bounded-order baseline moments but no linear decoder, below every fixed target trigger. Thus neither graph-only covers nor a fixed-order scale-free energy increment can replace the label-aware alternative.
messages.subject: Graph-only alternatives remain insufficient

messages.body_markdown: A useful additional direct certificate is `IE-L-TEMPLATE-POPULARITY`: if already-extracted exact templates carry mass $\delta$ and their number is at most $\delta(p+1)$, one template has agreement at least $\delta/4$. This consumes a template partition rather than extracting it, so it complements rather than proves the bounded-weight rank alternative.
messages.subject: Template-popularity decoder branch

nodes.label: Accepted-incidence graph
nodes.notes: All measures use the uniform point-line incidence normalization in the fixed prime-field, bivariate scope.
nodes.statement_markdown: Fix a prime $p$, an integer $100<d<p$, a function $f:\mathbb F_p^2\to\mathbb F_p$, and one polynomial $P_L\in\mathbb F_p[t]$ of degree at most $d$ for each affine line $L$, with a fixed bijective affine parametrization $L:\mathbb F_p\to L$. Define $$E_{\rm acc}=\{(L(t),L):P_L(t)=f(L(t))\},\qquad \epsilon=\frac{|E_{\rm acc}|}{p^2(p+1)},$$ and $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)=\max_{\deg_{\rm tot}Q\le d}\Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)].$$ For $G=(X,T,E)\subseteq E_{\rm acc}$ put $$e(G)=\frac{|E|}{p^2(p+1)},\quad \mu(G)=\frac{|X|}{p^2},\quad \tau(G)=\frac{|T|}{p(p+1)},$$ and write $\deg_X(G)$ and $\deg_T(G)$ for its point- and line-side minimum degrees.

nodes.label: Rank-reaching structured family
nodes.notes: This records label-aware linear rank, not merely the number of selected lines.
nodes.statement_markdown: For $D\ge d$ let $$V_D=\{A\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]:\operatorname{wdeg}_{(1,1,d)}A\le D\}$$ and $$\Phi_{R,D}:V_D\to\bigoplus_{M\in R}\mathbb F_p[t]_{\le D},\qquad A\mapsto\bigl(A(M(t),P_M(t))\bigr)_{M\in R}.$$ For $G=(X,T,E)$ define $$\operatorname{Reach}_R^G(L)=\{x:(x,L)\in E,\ \exists M\in R\setminus\{L\},\ (x,M)\in E\}.$$ The tuple $(G,R,D)$ is rank-reaching if $R\subseteq T$, $|R|>D$, $$\operatorname{rank}\Phi_{R,D}<\dim V_D,$$ and $|\operatorname{Reach}_R^G(L)|>D$ for every $L\in T$.

nodes.label: Accepted point-popularity tail
nodes.notes: The tail measures accepted edge mass supported on points of large full accepted degree.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Let $$a_x=|\{L:(x,L)\in E_{\rm acc}\}|,
\qquad \delta_j=\frac{1}{p^2(p+1)}\sum_{x:a_x\ge j}a_x,$$ and, when $\epsilon>0$, define $$u_*=\max\{1\le j\le p+1:\delta_j\ge\epsilon/2\}.$$

nodes.label: High-tail asymmetric core
nodes.notes: The source step is exact-indexed but conditional and has enclosing audit verdict revise.
nodes.statement_markdown:
If $$u_*\epsilon^2\ge2^{70}d,$$ then the tail supported on $\{x:a_x\ge u_*\}$ contains a nonempty accepted graph $G_*$ with point minimum degree $u$, line minimum degree $v$, line measure $\tau$, and $w=\min\{u,v\}$ satisfying $$u\ge u_*/3,\qquad v\ge\epsilon p/16,$$ $$uv\ge2^{60}dp,
\qquad uw^2\ge2^{60}d\tau p^2.$$

nodes.label: Near-lossless asymmetric reaching sample
nodes.notes: The statement is general; the critical path applies it to the tail core. The enclosing audit verdict is revise.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Let $G=(X,T,E)$ be nonempty with point minimum $u$, line minimum $v$, $t=|T|$, line measure $\tau$, and $w=\min\{u,v\}$. If $$uv\ge2^{60}dp,
\qquad uw^2\ge2^{60}d\tau p^2,$$ then $$\tau\ge\frac{u}{4(p+1)},\qquad \mu(G)\ge\frac{v}{4p},\qquad w^2\ge2^{57}dp,$$ and there is $R\subseteq T$ such that $$\frac{4t}{u}\le|R|\le\frac{16t}{u},\qquad |R|\ge p,$$ and $$|\operatorname{Reach}_R^G(L)|>\frac12\deg_G(L)$$ for every $L\in T$.

nodes.label: Asymmetric incidence decoder
nodes.notes: This is a provisional generalization of the accepted symmetric component decoder; the source audit verdict is revise.
nodes.statement_markdown: Under the hypotheses of `IE-L-ASYMMETRIC-SAMPLE`, there exists one $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ with $\deg_{\rm tot}Q\le d$ and $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge\frac{v}{800p}.$$

nodes.label: High-popularity-tail decoder
nodes.notes: This isolates the new direct branch without claiming that the required tail lower bound is automatic.
nodes.statement_markdown: If $$u_*\epsilon^2\ge2^{70}d,$$ then one total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial satisfies $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge\frac{\epsilon}{12800}.$$

nodes.label: Reduce to the low-tail regime
nodes.notes: This strictly narrows the unresolved incidence problem in round 3.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every instance with $\epsilon>0$, either `IE-T-POPULARITY-DECODE` applies or $$u_*\epsilon^2<2^{70}d.$$ Hence a rank-or-decode lemma proved under the latter inequality suffices for the unrestricted target.

nodes.label: Residual bounded-weight rank-or-decode dichotomy
nodes.notes: This is the only genuinely new incidence obligation on the critical path. Graph-only reaching obstructions make the direct-decoder alternative essential.
nodes.statement_markdown:
For every fixed $0<\theta\le1/4$ there exist $C_\theta\ge1$, $0<a_\theta\le1$, and $K_\theta\ge1$ such that, whenever $$\epsilon\ge C_\theta\left(\frac dp\right)^{1-\theta},
\qquad u_*\epsilon^2<2^{70}d,$$ either $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge a_\theta\epsilon,$$ or there exist $G=(X,T,E)\subseteq E_{\rm acc}$, $R\subseteq T$, and $d\le D\le K_\theta d$ such that $$e(G)\ge a_\theta\epsilon$$ and $(G,R,D)$ is rank-reaching.

nodes.label: Near-lossless parameter gate
nodes.notes: The threshold constant may be enlarged without weakening the obligation.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Enlarge $C_\theta$ so that $C_\theta\ge16K_\theta/a_\theta$. In the structured branch, with $\rho=d/p$, $$\rho\le\frac{\epsilon}{C_\theta},
\qquad \frac Dp\le\frac{K_\theta}{C_\theta}\epsilon\le\frac{a_\theta\epsilon}{16},
\qquad D<p,$$ and therefore $$\frac{D^2}{p^2}+\frac{3D}{p}\le\frac{a_\theta\epsilon}{4}.$$

nodes.label: Low-rank squarefree interpolation
nodes.notes: The accepted source supplies the interpolation template; the rank-deficient input is the new upstream interface.
nodes.statement_markdown:
In the structured branch there is a nonzero squarefree $A\in V_D$ such that $$A_Z\not\equiv0,
\qquad A(M(t),P_M(t))\equiv0$$ for every $M\in R$. Indeed, radicalizing a nonzero kernel element preserves these line identities; $|R|>D$ excludes a $Z$-independent radical, and $D<p$ excludes a nonconstant $p$th-power dependence on $Z$.

nodes.label: Reached-root extension
nodes.notes: The cited accepted step gives the exact root-counting mechanism.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every $L\in T$, the more than $D$ distinct points in $\operatorname{Reach}_R^G(L)$ are roots of the degree-at-most-$D$ polynomial $A(L(t),P_L(t))$. Hence $$A(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0$$ for every line vertex $L$ of $G$.

nodes.label: Primitive separable reduction
nodes.notes: Both cited building blocks have accepted audits.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Write $A=HB$, where $H\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ is the coefficient content, $h=\deg H$, and $B$ is primitive in $Z$. Put $\delta=\operatorname{wdeg}_{(1,1,d)}B$. Then $B$ is squarefree and $Z$-dependent, $$d\le\delta,
\qquad h+\delta\le D<pd,
\qquad \gcd(B,B_Z)=1.$$ At most $h$ affine lines have $H|_L\equiv0$; every other line vertex satisfies $B(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0$.

nodes.label: Weighted vertical cleanup count
nodes.notes: The strongest exact triple has enclosing verdict revise; the separability and resultant building blocks are independently accepted.

nodes.label: Near-lossless global cleanup and peeling
nodes.notes: Every peeled edge is charged once to the vertex removed at that stage.
nodes.statement_markdown:
After vertical cleanup, repeatedly remove each point or line vertex of current degree at most $D$. Peeling costs less than $2D/p$, so `IE-R-LOW-WEIGHT-GATE` leaves a nonempty $G_1$ satisfying $$e(G_1)\ge\frac{a_\theta}{2}\epsilon,
\qquad \deg_X(G_1)>D,
\qquad \deg_T(G_1)>D.$$ Every remaining line obeys $B(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0$, and every remaining point obeys $$B(x,f(x))=0,
\qquad B_Z(x,f(x))\ne0.$$

nodes.label: Degree-preserving simple-root factor partition
nodes.notes: The accepted P7 step supplies simple-root end assignment; the factor-count input has enclosing audit verdict revise.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Factor $$B=c\prod_{i=1}^s C_i$$ into distinct irreducibles and put $\Delta_i=\operatorname{wdeg}(C_i)$. Primitivity makes every $C_i$ depend on $Z$, so $$s\le\deg_ZB\le D/d\le K_\theta.$$ At every simple point exactly one factor vanishes, and every incident surviving line has the same unique factor identity. Thus $G_1$ is the disjoint union of factor classes preserving all vertex degrees. Some class $F$ and factor $C$ satisfy $$e(F)\ge\frac{a_\theta}{2K_\theta}\epsilon,
\qquad \deg_X(F),\deg_T(F)>D\ge\Delta,$$ together with $$C(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0,
\qquad C(x,f(x))=0,
\qquad C_Z(x,f(x))\ne0$$ on their respective vertices.

nodes.label: Seed-point factor linearization
nodes.notes: The mathematical mechanism is exact-audited only under an enclosing revise verdict; a clean standalone resubmission remains desirable. No rejected source is cited.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Let $C\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]$ be irreducible and $Z$-dependent with $$\Delta=\operatorname{wdeg}_{(1,1,d)}C\le D<p.$$ Suppose one accepted seed $(b,\alpha)$ satisfies $$C(b,\alpha)=0,
\qquad C_Z(b,\alpha)\ne0,$$ and is incident to more than $\Delta$ distinct affine lines, reparametrized by $L(0)=b$, such that $$P_L(0)=\alpha,
\qquad C(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0.$$ Then there are $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ with $\deg_{\rm tot}Q\le d$ and $u\in\mathbb F_p^\times$ such that $$C=u(Z-Q).$$ Every point of the factor class in `IE-L-FACTOR-CONCENTRATE` supplies such a seed.

nodes.label: Vinh-free global factor aggregation
nodes.notes: Association to one fixed factor aggregates disconnected factor components without any incidence-mixing step.
nodes.statement_markdown:
For the class $F$ and factor $C$ from `IE-L-FACTOR-CONCENTRATE`, $C=u(Z-Q)$ and $C(x,f(x))=0$ imply $Q(x)=f(x)$ at every point vertex of $F$. Since every affine point is incident to at most $p+1$ lines, $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge\frac{|X(F)|}{p^2}\ge e(F)
\ge\frac{a_\theta}{2K_\theta}\epsilon.$$

nodes.label: Close high-tail, direct, and structured branches
nodes.notes: The only unproved critical-path input is the residual bounded-weight dichotomy; work states do not assert verifier status.
nodes.statement_markdown: Fix $\eta>0$ and put $\theta=\min\{\eta,1/4\}$. Since $0<d/p<1$, $$(d/p)^{1-\eta}\ge(d/p)^{1-\theta}.$$ Taking $C_\eta=C_\theta$ and $$c_\eta=\min\left\{\frac1{12800},a_\theta,\frac{a_\theta}{2K_\theta}\right\}$$ closes respectively the high-tail, residual direct-decoder, and structured-factor branches.

nodes.label: Near-linear bivariate line-versus-point soundness
nodes.notes: The recovered object is one global bivariate polynomial, not a component-dependent list.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every fixed $\eta>0$ there exist $C_\eta,c_\eta>0$ such that, for every prime $p$, integer $100<d<p$, function $f:\mathbb F_p^2\to\mathbb F_p$, and degree-at-most-$d$ affine-line table, $$\epsilon\ge C_\eta\left(\frac dp\right)^{1-\eta}$$ implies the existence of one $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ with $\deg_{\rm tot}Q\le d$ and $$\Pr_{x\in\mathbb F_p^2}[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge c_\eta\epsilon.$$

nodes.label: Baseline two-sided popularity pruning
nodes.notes: This remains a useful optional entry point, but the residual rank certificate does not require an induced whole-line core. The enclosing audit verdict is revise.
nodes.statement_markdown:
If an accepted carrier $G$ has $e(G)=\delta>0$ and $\tau(G)\le\sigma$, then it contains $G_0$ with $$e(G_0)\ge\delta/4,
\qquad \deg_X(G_0),\deg_T(G_0)\ge\left\lfloor\frac{\delta p}{100}\right\rfloor,
\qquad \delta/4\le\tau(G_0)\le\sigma.$$

nodes.label: Accepted component concentration and sampling
nodes.notes: Both source steps have accepted audits and give the cardinality-based baseline.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Let $G$ be connected with common minimum degree $k$, line measure $\tau$, and $t=|T|$. If $$k^2\ge2^{40}dp,
\qquad k^3\ge2^{40}d\tau p^2,$$ then $$\mu(G),\tau\ge\frac{k}{4p},$$ and there is $R\subseteq T$ with $$\frac{4t}{k}\le|R|\le\frac{16t}{k},
\qquad |\operatorname{Reach}_R^G(L)|>\frac12\deg_G(L)$$ for every $L\in T$.

nodes.label: Accepted component decoder
nodes.notes: The entire cited chain has an accepted audit.
nodes.statement_markdown: Under `IE-L-COMP-SAMPLE`, one $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ with $\deg_{\rm tot}Q\le d$ satisfies $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge\frac{k}{800p}.$$

nodes.label: Component-support square-root ceiling
nodes.notes: This diagnoses the cardinality/root-budget architecture, not the target theorem.
nodes.statement_markdown: If $0<k\le C\epsilon p$, $\tau\ge k/(4p)$, and $$k^3\ge C_*d\tau p^2,$$ then $$\epsilon^2\ge\frac{C_*}{4C^2}\frac dp.$$ Thus component-support localization alone cannot pass the square-root scale.

nodes.label: Exact-template popularity decoder
nodes.notes: This consumes an already-extracted template partition; it does not construct one. The enclosing audit verdict is revise.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let disjoint line families $T_1,\ldots,T_r$ carry total accepted mass $\delta$ and total line measure $\tau$, and suppose every $L\in T_j$ satisfies $$P_L(t)\equiv Q_j(L(t))$$ for some $Q_j$ of total degree at most $d$. If $$\alpha=\max_j\Pr_x[Q_j(x)=f(x)],$$ then $$\delta\le\alpha\tau+\sqrt{\frac{r\alpha\tau}{p+1}}.$$ In particular, $r\le\delta(p+1)$ implies $\alpha\ge\delta/4$.

nodes.label: Integral reaching-cover obstruction
nodes.notes: The accepted construction rules out a universal smaller graph-only selector, not soundness.
nodes.statement_markdown: For $p\ge103$ and $2\le K\le p/(100\log p)$ there is a legal table with $$\frac1{2K}\le\epsilon\le\frac2K$$ such that every line subset reaching half of every accepted line has size $$|R|\ge\frac{Kp}{16}\ge\frac{p}{32\epsilon},$$ while a constant polynomial has agreement at least $\epsilon/2$.

nodes.label: Connected fractional reaching obstruction
nodes.notes: The bound concerns the optimum total weight, not every feasible weight assignment. The enclosing audit verdict is revise.
nodes.statement_markdown: There is a connected, full-support legal table with $\epsilon=d/p$, every line of accepted degree $d$, every point of accepted degree $d$ or $d+1$, and perfect decoder $Q=0$. For $0<\vartheta\le1$, let $\operatorname{OPT}_\vartheta$ be the minimum $\sum_M\lambda_M$ over $\lambda_M\ge0$ satisfying, for every line $L$, $$\sum_{x\in N(L)}\min\left\{1,\sum_{\substack{M\ne L\\x\in N(M)}}\lambda_M\right\}\ge\vartheta d.$$ Then $$\frac{\vartheta p(p+1)}{d+1}\le\operatorname{OPT}_\vartheta\le\frac{\vartheta p(p+1)}{d-1}=\Theta\left(\frac p\epsilon\right).$$

nodes.label: Exact all-order star identity
nodes.notes: At density $\epsilon\asymp1/p$, regularity need not imply $\Gamma_2=\Theta(\epsilon^2)$. The source audit verdict is revise.
nodes.statement_markdown: For $2\le s\le p+1$, define the ordered distinct-line star density $$\Gamma_s=\frac{1}{p^2(p+1)_s}\sum_x(a_x)_s.$$ Then $$\Gamma_2=\epsilon^2-\frac{\epsilon(1-\epsilon)}p+ rac{\operatorname{Var}_x(a_x)}{p(p+1)}.$$

nodes.label: Bounded-order star-energy obstruction
nodes.notes: These examples lie below every fixed $(d/p)^{1-\eta}$ trigger and therefore do not refute the campaign target.
nodes.statement_markdown:
For every fixed $S$ and all sufficiently large primes $p$, there is a legal instance with $d=101$ such that $$\epsilon=\Theta\left(\frac{\log p}{p\log\log p}\right),
\qquad \operatorname{Agr}_{101}(f)<\frac2p,$$ every affine line supports acceptance, and $$\Gamma_s=O_S(\epsilon^s)
\qquad(2\le s\le S).$$ Thus no fixed-order, scale-free star-energy increment can replace the decoder branch.

nodes.label: Compatibility-graph DRC with concurrency correction
nodes.notes: This is an exact diagnostic for auxiliary line graphs; the enclosing audit verdict is revise.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Let $H$ have the $N=p(p+1)$ affine lines as vertices, joining $L\ne M$ when both accept their intersection. With $\mu=(p+1)\epsilon$ and average degree $\bar\Delta$, $$e(H)=\sum_x\binom{a_x}{2},
\qquad \bar\Delta\ge\frac{p\mu(\mu-1)}{p+1}.$$ For $1\le t\le\lfloor\bar\Delta\rfloor$, some distinct $t$-line seed has at least $$M_t(H)\ge N\frac{\binom{\lfloor\bar\Delta\rfloor}{t}}{\binom Nt}$$ common neighbors; if $\mu\ge2$ and $\bar\Delta\ge2t+2$, this is at least $N(\epsilon^2/4)^t$. Among them, at least $$M_t(H)-\frac{\binom t2(p+1)}{t-h+1}$$ meet the seed lines in at least $h$ distinct points.

nodes.label: Density-only DRC root-budget barrier
nodes.notes: This only limits the displayed density-only certificate; it is not an impossibility theorem for auxiliary-graph methods.
nodes.statement_markdown: Put $$D_t=16(\lfloor\sqrt{dt}\rfloor+1).$$ A transfer requiring $h>D_t$ with $h\le t$ forces $t>D_t$ and hence $t>256d$. At fixed $d,t$ and $$\epsilon=C(d/p)^{1/3},$$ the density term $N(\epsilon^2/4)^t$ tends to zero. Taking $h=D_t+1$, the concurrency correction in `IE-L-AUXILIARY-DRC` makes the resulting lower bound eventually negative, so this estimate alone supplies no root-rich target at the cubic scale.

summary: Round 3 adds the asymmetric popularity-tail chain from researcher-0010. A high tail $u_*\epsilon^2\ge2^{70}d$ yields a two-sided core, a $\Theta(|T|/u)$ reaching sample, and one decoder with agreement $\epsilon/12800$; the central incidence obligation is therefore restricted to the complementary low-tail regime. Accepted component sampling remains a square-root-scale baseline. Exact cover constructions, bounded-order star examples, and concurrency-corrected auxiliary DRC show why graph-only selectors, fixed-order energy increments, and the displayed density-only DRC certificate cannot establish the near-linear target. The residual obligation must instead output either a decoder or a label-aware rank-reaching relation of mass $\Omega_\theta(\epsilon)$ and weight $D=O_\theta(d)$. That bound makes cleanup loss $O_\theta(d/p)$ absorbable and leaves only $O_\theta(1)$ irreducible factors. The downstream squarefree interpolation, vertical cleanup, factor partition, seed-only factor linearization, and disconnected-factor aggregation then recover one global polynomial. The factor lift has exact revise-grade support and needs a clean standalone audit; the bounded-weight residual dichotomy is the only genuinely new mathematical bottleneck. Work states report activity only.
target_statement: Convert local line-versus-point agreement into a structured affine-plane incidence configuration with only a $(d/p)^{o(1)}$ loss.
title: Incidence concentration engine
